preconditions.means: The catalog name is unique to glovashu, so a fully-qualified read that succeeds could only have been answered by glovashu.

statements.name: create_catalog
statements.sql: CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS awoz1227_glovashu

statements.name: create_schema
statements.sql: CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS awoz1227_glovashu.opensharing_provider

statements.name: create_table
statements.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE awoz1227_glovashu.opensharing_provider.test_dataset ( record_id BIGINT, agency_name STRING, use_case STRING, region STRING, record_date DATE, metric_value DOUBLE, origin_metastore STRING, internal_notes STRING )

statements.name: insert_rows
statements.sql: INSERT INTO awoz1227_glovashu.opensharing_provider.test_dataset SELECT id, element_at(array('Agency Delta','Agency Echo', 'Agency Foxtrot'), CAST((id % 3) + 1 AS INT)), 'CONOPS 2.4.1 D2D ingress demo', element_at(array('eu-west','eu-north','eu-south'), CAST((id % 3) + 1 AS INT)), date_add(current_date(), CAST(-id AS INT)), round(rand() * 1000, 2), '8875961b-9666-494c-95e2-af6b5b78bd3d', 'synthetic

verification.query: SELECT count(*) AS n, count(DISTINCT origin_metastore) AS n_origins, min(origin_metastore) AS origin FROM awoz1227_glovashu.opensharing_provider.test_dataset
verification.means: A SUCCEEDED INSERT says the statement ran. These three say the rows exist, carry one origin, and that the origin is the metastore we read the id from -- so a T-19 read that returns these rows can only have been answered by glovashu.
